correctness.rationale: Left translation by a group element preserves rank and normalizes the support to {1,h,h²,w} for a reflection w. The left convolution on each right coset of <h,w> is an identical 2m-dimensional operator, giving the multiplier N/m. Independently using the cyclic Fourier basis, at each m-th root z pair sum_k z^(-k)h^k with sum_k z^k h^k w: h acts with eigenvalues z,z^(-1), and w swaps them. Each pair has determinant Q(z+z^(-1)), with Q(t)=ac t²+b(a+c)t+(a-c)²+b²-d². Since d≠0, a singular pair contributes exactly one; traces at ±2 have one preimage when present and interior traces two. Since ac≠0, at most two traces vanish; there is only one interior trace at m=3,4, and at least two for m≥5. The two explicit coefficient constructions prescribe any desired distinct trace roots, including opposite pairs, without a zero tap; adding roots outside [-2,2] attains 0, 1 and 2, while one endpoint and one interior root attain 3 and two interior roots attain 4 where available. For the count, two possible progression centers p,q with third point r would satisfy 2p=q+r and 2q=p+r, forcing 3(p-q)=0; the step then has order 3. Order-three triples are subgroup cosets with three centers and two orientations each, while all higher orders have one center and two orientations. This gives the census and disjointness for all H in scope.

value.rationale: The support embeds the smallest rotational progression with both cosets represented, a natural sparsity class. A user of regular convolution can now tell which losses of rank are possible on each fixed support, including exactly where the fourth packet first becomes possible and how identical subgroup components amplify rank loss. The accompanying incidence count answers how often each step order arises, independently of the rank calculation. This is a complete classification across all orders, not a re-computation of the known small case.
residual_risks: No result on non-progression support, condition numbers, eigenvalue gaps, or equal-weight coefficients follows.
